text:
Gandalf (1), your birds stay dark while the bazaar wakes. Either feed them or say when the lamps will catch flame; a lantern unlit is a shadow unpaid.

Elsa (7), the Potter’s rot stinks louder than your silence. Name the creditor or tell the village why you let Potter’s rot fester—yes or no.

Gandalf (1), your censer still smokes with incense unpaid while your birds perch in silence. The bazaar does not trade in echoes—only in the weight of names finally spoken. Do you feed your birds daily, or is the ledger’s blank page your true creditor? Yes or no.

Elsa (7), your inkwell beads like Potter’s rot, yet the creditor’s name stays locked in your silence. You stir the stench as if it might reveal the pattern, but a ledger without ink is a debt unpaid—name the hand that wrote it. Yes or no.
